prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
U0001: 1 INTRODUCTION PURPOSE NASA’s future exploration missions mandate a significant paradigm change for mission planning, spacecraft design, human systems integration, and in-flight medical care due to constraints on mass, volume, power, resupply missions, and medical evacuation capabilities.
U0002: These constraints require further development of the human health and performance system, which includes the medical, task performance, wellness, data, human and other systems necessary to keep the crew healthy and functioning optimally [1, 2, 3].
U0003: The human health and performance system will be tightly integrated with mission and habitat design to provide a sufficient human health and performance infrastructure to enable mission success.
U0004: A suite of systems engineering tools will aid in the decision making process for the development of such a human health and performance system.
U0005: This Concept of Operations provides a vision for a tool suite to conduct evaluations of human health and performance system options, inform research prioritization, and provide trade study support, based on evidence, risks, and systems engineering principles.
U0006: The integrated tool suite under development is IMPACT.
U0007: SCOPE This Concept of Operations will be used to guide the development of IMPACT.
U0008: It also provides an overview of the stakeholder need and system goals of IMPACT, as well as examples of the types of activities for which the system can be used during the development of these missions.
U0009: The document outlines the functions and data that are needed for IMPACT.
U0010: CHANGE AUTHORITY This version of the Concept of Operations will be controlled by the Exploration Medical Capability (ExMC) Control Board.
U0011: If programs outside of ExMC choose to utilize and change the content in this document, any changes must be communicated to ExMC leadership, and the changes must be processed through the respective control boards.
U0012: APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS Table 1-1 below includes documents that contain provisions or other pertinent requirements directly related to and necessary for the performance of the activities specified by this Concept of Operations.
U0013: They also contain supplemental information and provide guidance in the application of the Concept of Operations document.
U0014: These documents may or may not be specifically cited within the text of this document.
U0015: Document Number Title N/A Systems Engineering Management Plan (SEMP) Table 1-1: Applicable Documents 2 STAKEHOLDER NEED & SYSTEM GOALS IMPACT is being developed for ExMC to address the medical system, but the tool suite concept can be extended to suit the needs of other Human Research Program Elements.
U0016: Other potential stakeholders of IMPACT include, but are not limited to: • Human Research Program (HRP) o HRP Management o ExMC Leadership o Other HRP Element Leadership • Medical Operations (MedOps) • Program Management o Program Systems Engineering Team o Crew Health and Performance (CHP) System Management o Medical System Management • The Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer (OCHMO) • Human System Risk Board (HSRB) • Health and Medical Technical Authority (HMTA) STAKEHOLDER NEED The need for IMPACT is to provide a data-driven means to inform human health and performance risk mitigation interests during resource-constrained exploration mission development.
U0017: GOALS 2.2.1 Enable systematic trade study evaluations IMPACT will provide trade study evaluations to aid stakeholders in making informed decisions.
U0018: These trade studies are systematic evaluations of data needed to create candidate system options and include the assessment of requirements satisfaction, resource figures of merit (i.e., mass, volume, technology readiness level (TRLs)), and risk metrics (i.e., probability of loss of crew life). 2.2.2 Inform Research Prioritization IMPACT will provide the quantification of the effect of proposed research on risk reduction, allowing stakeholders to prioritize funding.
U0019: For example, IMPACT can be used to determine the benefit of funding development of a new piece of technology.
